ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier negative feedback circuit. The input signal Vi is connected to the non-inverting input terminal (+) of the op-amp. The inverting input terminal (−) is grounded through R1=1 kΩ, and is connected to the output terminal Vo through the feedback resistor R2=79 kΩ. Therefore this is a non-inverting amplifier structure, and the feedback coefficient is determined by resistor voltage division. Reasoning: The feedback coefficient beta = R1/(R1+R2) = 1 kΩ/(1 kΩ+79 kΩ) = 1/80 = 0.0125. The problem gives the compensated op-amp open-loop low-frequency gain Ao=10^5, and the open-loop cutoff frequency fc=8 Hz. At f=15 kHz, the single-pole open-loop gain model is A(jf)=10^5/(1+j f/fc)=10^5/(1+j 15000/8)=10^5/(1+j1875). The closed-loop non-inverting amplifier gain is Vo/Vi = A/(1+beta A), and its magnitude is |Vo/Vi|=|A|/|1+beta A|. Calculation gives A≈0.02844−j53.333, beta A≈0.0003556−j0.66667, so 1+beta A≈1.000356−j0.66667. Thus |A|≈53.333, |1+beta A|≈1.202, and the closed-loop gain magnitude ≈53.333/1.202≈44.4 V/V.
